question: Why do electric cars slow their fast charging when the battery is cold, though cold cells cannot overheat?
answer: Because cold graphite takes lithium in too slowly. Ions arriving faster than they can slip between the carbon layers settle on its surface as metallic lithium, a plating that locks away capacity and can grow spikes. So cars warm the pack first: choosing a fast charger as the destination often switches the battery heater on.
move: A process that is safe when slow can turn harmful at speed.
source: Petzl et al., Journal of Power Sources, 2015
reference: Petzl, Kasper & Danzer, Lithium plating in a commercial lithium-ion battery: A low-temperature aging study, Journal of Power Sources, 2015
